A long number is split into several pieces in a not very predictable way, and that is why models find arithmetic harder than would seem reasonable: “127” may be a single piece and “128” two. The same explains why they fail at counting the letters of a word that to them is a single indivisible symbol, or at writing backwards. It is not that they cannot think: it is that they do not see the letters you are asking them to count.
